title: Chicken Teriyaki
subtitle: Sticky glazed chicken thighs in a Japanese-style sauce
excerpt: Teriyaki sauce thickens and caramelises in the pan as it cooks, coating the chicken in a glossy, sticky glaze. A short marinade adds depth. Serve over steamed rice with the pan juices spooned over.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking technique where food is grilled or pan-fried in a soy, mirin, and sake glaze. The word combines teri, meaning gloss, and yaki, meaning grilled. The technique is recorded in Japanese cookbooks from the seventeenth century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight for a deeper flavour.

content.text: Use a non-stick pan or the glaze will catch and burn before the chicken is cooked through. Keep the heat at medium once the sauce goes in.
Mix together the marinade ingredients in a bowl.
Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lift the chicken from the marinade. Reserve the marinade.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat with a little oil.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes on each side until cooked through.
Pour the reserved marinade into the pan. Let it bubble and reduce for 2 to 3 minutes until it coats the chicken in a thick glaze.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Glaze burns before chicken is done.
items.cause: Heat too high when sauce was added.
items.fix: Turn down to medium when you add the marinade.

items.cause: Too much marinade or heat too low.
items.fix: Increase heat slightly and simmer uncovered until glossy.

items.cause: Thighs were thick or not at room temperature.
items.fix: Use a probe thermometer. Internal temperature must reach 74C.
